1201-program-description: Specialized physical geography. Besides CGPA 3.00, keep a program GPA of 3.30 and do a 6-credit Honours thesis.
1201-complementary-courses-45-credits: 9 on human-environment links, 3 of statistics (see Course Overlap), 9 of systematic physical geography, 3 of field courses, 15 across environmental analysis and Environment, Earth Science and Sustainability (9 and 6 either way), and 6 of approved advanced courses.
1203-about-immunology: A demanding Honours from three departments, preparing you for graduate immunology. If you lose Honours Standing, transfer to a program in one of them. See program advisors.
1203-location: Physiology: McIntyre, Room 1136. Coordinators: Dr. Heather Melichar, Dr. Judith Mandl, Dr. Ana Nijnik. Microbiology and Immunology: Duff, Room 511.
1203-program-description: With Biochemistry, Microbiology and Immunology, and Physiology, on the pathophysiology of immune diseases. 48 required and 27 complementary credits.
Graduate with CGPA 3.30 and at least B in MIMM 214, MIMM 314, PHGY 531, PHGY 419D1/D2, PHGY 513, and one of BIOC 503, MIMM 414 or MIMM 509.
1203-u1: BIOC 212 or BIOL 201. PHGY 209 or MIMM 211.
1204-u1: 3 and 3 from two lists. CHEM 203 or 204. PHGY 209 or MIMM 211.
1204-u2: 6 of labs: BIOC 220 and 320, or the Immunology lab, or Physiology Lab 2 with BIOL 301. 6 from the list. BIOL 309 or MATH 315, not both.
1204-u3-2: 3 and 6 from two lists. ANAT 458 or BIOC 458, not both.
1208-about-kinesiology-for-science-stude: For future health professionals and researchers: physical activity for health, and exercise in treating disease, injury and disability, for prevention and rehabilitation. Only the Minor's 18 EDKP credits are allowed.
1208-location: Currie Gymnasium, 475 Pine Ave. W., 2nd Floor, H2W 1S4.
1208-program-description: The science of physical activity, health and well-being. Limited, by application. No extra courses outside Arts and Science.
1209-management-for-science-students: Science students may apply to the Management Minor (p. 1209), or take the Entrepreneurship Minor (p. 1191), which excludes Desautels' Finance, Management, Marketing and Operations minors.
1211-program-description: With any non-Mathematics Science program. Declare at the start of your second-last year, with the Chief Adviser approving courses. MATH 323 is strongly recommended; others from major and honours courses without duplication, or up to 6 from other departments.
Overlap with your primary program: 6 credits, or with approved courses, 9 if it's 60+ credits and 12 if it's 72+.
1211-required-courses-9-credits: MATH 235 and 236 may replace MATH 223, reducing complementary credits by 3.
1211-complementary-courses-15-credits: From major and honours courses, MATH 323 strongly recommended; up to 6 from other departments.
1211-program-description-2: 24–27 credits, with any Science program not mainly Statistics. Declare at the start of your second-last year, with the Chief Adviser's approval. C or better. Overlap: 6 credits, or with approved courses, 9 if your program is 60+ credits and 12 if it's 72+.
1212-complementary-courses-9-12-credits: No more than 6 from outside the department.
1212-program-description: A general overview of mathematics, with rigorous foundations and its branches.
1212-program-prerequisites: Normally completed beforehand; otherwise add them on top of the 45 credits.
1212-guidelines-for-selection-of-courses: Talk to your adviser. Honours courses may replace Major ones, and are encouraged if you're heading to graduate school. There are suggested lists for computer science (with the CS Minor), probability and statistics, applied math, secondary teaching, and business, industry or government.
1213-required-courses-27-credits: With an equivalent of MATH 222, replace it with 3 complementary credits. MATH 249 or 316, not both.
1214-program-description: Statistics with a math core and basic computing. Strong results in the right courses can lead to A.Stat. from the Statistical Society of Canada, the entry-level credential for statisticians. 45 or 48 credits.
1214-required-courses-27-credits: If you can program, replace COMP 202 with COMP 250 or 350. MATH 204 before MATH 324. With an equivalent of MATH 222, take 3 complementary credits instead.
1214-complementary-courses-18-or-21-cred: Without MATH 203's equivalent, see an adviser and take it first term, making 48. 6+ from one list (MATH 317 or COMP 350) and 9+ from another. At most one of MATH 410, 420, 527D1/D2 and WCOM 314.
1215-program-description: A general overview of mathematics, with rigorous foundations and its branches.
1215-program-prerequisites: Normally completed beforehand; otherwise add them on top of the 54 credits.
1216-required-courses-27-credits: If you did well in MATH 235 and 242, consider Honours through MATH 251 and 255 instead of 236 and 243. With an equivalent of MATH 222, take 3 complementary credits instead. MATH 249 or 316, not both.
1216-complementary-courses-27-credits: 6–12 from one list and 15–21 from another, 6+ at 400–500. If needed, 6 more in math or related fields with the Adviser.
1217-program-description: Statistics with a math core and basic computing, possibly leading to A.Stat. accreditation. 54–57 credits.
1217-program-prerequisites: Normally completed beforehand; otherwise add them on top of the 54 credits. Without MATH 203's equivalent, see an adviser; if needed, it's a first-term complementary, making 57.
Finish required and Part I courses by the end of U2, except MATH 423 and 523. Ask about accreditation. Honours courses may replace Major ones; for graduate school, take MATH 556 and 557.
1217-required-courses-34-credits: MATH 204 before MATH 324. With an equivalent of MATH 222, take MATH 314 instead.
1217-complementary-courses-20-23-credits: Part I: 6 credits (MATH 317 or COMP 350). Part II: 14 credits (COMP 451 or 551). At most one of MATH 410, 420, 527D1/D2 and WCOM 314.
1218-program-description: Core skills in both fields and how they interact.
1218-program-prerequisites: Normally completed beforehand; otherwise add them on top of the 72 credits.
1219-required-courses-54-credits: If you know a programming language, replace COMP 202 with a CS complementary. COMP 350 can't replace MATH 317.
1219-complementary-courses-18-credits: 9 of math (others with an adviser) and 9 of CS at 300+ (not COMP 396) or ECSE 508.
1219-program-description: Training in both, with the math behind them, for ever-growing data.
1220-required-courses-51-credits: If you know a programming language, replace COMP 202 with a CS complementary. COMP 350 or MATH 317. MATH 223 or 236, equal as prerequisites.
1220-complementary-courses-21-credits: 12 of math: MATH 204 before MATH 324, MATH 340 or 350, MATH 410 or 527D1/D2, and not both MATH 578 and COMP 540.
9 of CS: 6+ from the list, and the rest from COMP at 300+ (not COMP 396) and ECSE 508.
